title: Sales
description: Review the buyer, the purchase process and what Sales can substantiate in a conversation.
questions: Who uses, sponsors and approves the purchase?
Which buyer objections can the proposed change address with evidence?
What should Sales show in a demo or explain during procurement?

specialists.title: Sales discovery specialist
specialists.focus: Identify the customer's current process, cost of the problem and expected outcome. Choose questions that check assumptions without leading the buyer.

specialists.title: Opportunity qualification lead
specialists.focus: Separate user, sponsor, economic buyer and decision authority. Distinguish buyer-confirmed criteria and milestones from seller expectations.

specialists.title: Sales enablement lead
specialists.focus: Map known objections to evidence the seller can show. Design a demo around one buyer workflow and identify claims the demo cannot substantiate.

specialists.title: Procurement specialist
specialists.focus: Identify buyer-side procurement stages, technical and security documentation, dependencies and handoffs that can delay a decision.

evidence: Approved discovery or CRM records confirming the customer problem, stakeholder roles, expected outcomes and known alternatives.
Buyer-provided criteria, milestones or procurement documents with a named source and date. Label any seller estimates.
Current product documentation, demo environment and approved proof points for claims about available capabilities.
Agreed pricing, implementation and support boundaries from the responsible internal owners if they are relevant to the buyer conversation.
challenge: Compare a targeted demo, a discovery follow-up and pausing qualification. Identify the evidence that would justify each next step.
Test whether the apparent champion has access to the decision maker and whether budget, approval and procurement milestones come from the buyer.
Check that the demo uses the buyer's actual task and distinguishes released functions, planned work and elements shown only in the demo environment.
Challenge proposed dates or commitments that omit buyer-side approval, security review, implementation capacity or dependencies.
decision_criteria: Advance when the buyer confirms the problem, a relevant next milestone and who on their side owns it.
Keep in discovery when a decision criterion, stakeholder or business impact is still a seller assumption. Name the next question and who can answer it.
Recommend a demo or proof of value when it directly tests a buyer-confirmed criterion using approved evidence and realistic constraints.
Route terms, delivery guarantees and commitments outside the team's agreed scope to the responsible internal owner before quoting them.
